name: Lay out residential and small business services
summary: A homeowner, small business or their electrician asks the utility for a new, upgraded or relocated service of 50 kW or less. The service desk logs the request, a design technologist checks the supply transformer and secondary in the GIS, visits the site when needed, and issues a customer layout showing the supply point, meter location and charges. Once the customer pays and the electrician and trench contractor have finished, the trench is inspected and the technologist releases a work order to crew scheduling. Most of the elapsed time is waiting for the customer to decide and for the electrician's work; the utility's own delays are design queues in the spring and summer, missing information and failed trench inspections.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario distributor serving about 350,000 customers, with a central service desk, about 26 design technologists, GIS, an ERP for work orders and a customer information system.
baseline.notes: Process steps follow Hydro Ottawa's published service request, trench and Conditions of Service pages; volumes, minutes and waits are estimates.

trigger: A customer, electrician or the contact centre submits an electrical service request for a new, upgraded or relocated low-voltage service.
end_state: A paid layout has a construction work order released to work planning, or the customer has dropped the project or let the quote expire.

volume.seasonality: Requests rise from March to July ahead of the building season and fall in December and January.

evidence.note: 9,001 appointments for service upgrades, meter checks and service layouts in 2021 and 5,024 connections (scorecard); the organisation file's 330 to 600 requests a month assumes about 15% do not proceed and some connections come from developer projects instead. Kept as in the organisation file.

Organisation file role (40 people, extended hours). Service desk work on requests, payments and inspection bookings. FTE = expected minutes per case x 450 requests / 130 hours, plus 15% for follow-up calls.
Organisation file role (26 people). FTE = expected minutes per case x 450 requests / 130 hours, plus 15% for customer calls and revisions not tied to a step.
Organisation file role (4 people). Assignment and review minutes plus 50% for escalations and customer complaints.
Organisation file role (6 people), not listed for this process in the organisation file's process map; Hydro Ottawa inspects every underground service trench twice (trench page).

systems.name: Customer web portal, MyAccount, mobile app and outage map
Contact centre telephony, IVR and call recording
ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Document management and engineering drawing repository
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
Local meter data management and validation tool
Mobile workforce management and field tablets

resources.name: Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Receive the service request and check the form
steps.description: A customer service representative on the service desk opens the electrical service request that arrived through the web form or by email, and checks that it has the civic address, the service size, the electrician's details, the requested date and, for a new or relocated service, a site plan. Requests for more than 50 kW or five or more units are sent to the distribution design team instead.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Request form contents from the service request page; 50 kW and five-unit thresholds from the distribution design page; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Create the request in the customer and work order systems
steps.description: The representative finds the premise and account in the customer system, opens a design work request in the ERP with the premise number, and files the form and site plan in the document system so the designer sees one record. The same address and contact details are typed into both systems.

error.defect_description: Wrong premise picked or a duplicate request opened.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of re-keying between the customer system and the ERP common in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Assign the request to a design technologist
steps.description: The distribution design supervisor goes through new requests once a day, groups them by area and assigns each to the design technologist who covers that part of the city or rural area.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of a daily assignment batch.

steps.name: Review the request against the GIS and records
steps.description: The technologist opens the GIS to find the supply transformer or pole, the secondary bus and the existing service, checks the service history in the customer system and the request details, and decides whether a site visit is needed. Missing site plans or service sizes go back to the customer.

error.defect_description: Wrong supply transformer identified from an out-of-date GIS.

evidence.note: Hydro Ottawa calls within 10 business days and asks for requests three to four weeks before the project (service request page); DSC s.6.1.1 requires a response within 15 calendar days. Queue length is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Ask the customer for missing information
steps.description: The technologist emails or phones the customer or electrician for the missing site plan, service size or load summary and puts the request on hold.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Customer sends the missing information
steps.description: The customer or electrician sends the site plan, load summary or corrected service size by email, and the request goes back into the technologist's review queue.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Call the customer or electrician and book the site visit
steps.description: The technologist phones the customer or electrician to confirm what they want, explain the process and, when a visit is needed, book it within a four-hour window.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Distribution System Code s.6.1.1 (respond to a connection request within 15 calendar days) and s.7.3-7.4 (four-hour appointment window)

next.condition: desk layout from records and photos

evidence.note: Hydro Ottawa's first call within 10 business days (service request page); service layouts are among the appointments booked in four-hour windows (scorecard). Share needing a visit is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive to the site
steps.description: The technologist drives a utility light vehicle to the address, often combining two or three visits in one area on the same day.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of drive time and appointment lead time.

steps.name: Review the site with the customer
steps.description: On site the technologist confirms the supply point and route, marks the meter base location, checks clearances to buildings, pools and trees, measures the service length and photographs the existing service and transformer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: The utility designates the supply point and meter base location and assesses the service (Conditions of Service s.3.1.3; service request page). Minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check transformer and secondary loading
steps.description: The technologist adds the new or upgraded load to the transformer's connected customers using smart meter peaks and the load summary, and checks voltage drop on the secondary. An overloaded transformer or long secondary means an upgrade must be designed first.

error.defect_description: Load added to the wrong transformer.

evidence.note: The layout includes an assessment of the service loading (service request page); the share needing an upgrade is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Design the transformer or secondary upgrade
steps.description: The technologist designs the larger transformer or new secondary run, prepares a material list and checks whether the work needs an outage or a pole. Materials with long lead times are flagged so the customer is warned.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Hydro Ottawa notifies customers of extended lead times for special equipment (Conditions of Service s.2.1); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the customer layout and charges
steps.description: The technologist draws the layout sketch (supply point, meter base location, conductor size and route, trench specification for underground) and lists the customer's responsibilities and the charges from the standard fee tables, such as the shared transformer cost and service wire beyond 30 m.

error.defect_description: Wrong fee line or service length on the quote.

evidence.note: Layout contents and fee methodology from the Conditions of Service s.3.1.3 and Appendix G; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the layout and charges
steps.description: The design supervisor checks the layout and the charges, focusing on non-standard services, upgrades and quotes above the standard fees, and signs it off or sends it back.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Design checking: supervisor review of customer layouts and quoted charges

evidence.note: Author's estimate of a supervisory check common in design groups.

steps.name: Email the layout and quote to the customer
steps.description: The technologist emails the layout and quote to the customer and electrician with the validity date and the next steps: pay the fees, have the electrician take out the ESA permit, build the trench if underground, then call the service desk.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Layout sent by email; sequence of customer steps from the service request and trench pages.

steps.name: Customer accepts and pays
steps.description: The customer decides whether to go ahead and pays the layout charges by phone, online or cheque. Quotes expire after 90 days. Some customers ask for a change, such as a different meter location, and some drop the project.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

next.condition: does not proceed or the quote expires

evidence.note: Quotes expire after 90 days and one free layout per property per year (Conditions of Service Appendix G); shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Post the payment and notify the designer
steps.description: The representative records the payment against the request in the customer system and the ERP and emails the technologist that the job can proceed.

error.defect_description: Payment posted to the wrong request.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Electrician and contractor complete the customer's work
steps.description: The electrician takes out the ESA permit and installs the meter base, panel and mast, and for an underground service the customer's contractor gets locates and digs the trench with duct and rope to the utility's specification. This waiting time is the longest part of the process.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

next.condition: overhead service or upgrade without trench

evidence.note: Customer work sequence from the trench page and ESA's service inspection page; duration and underground share are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Book the trench inspections
steps.description: The contractor calls the service desk, and the representative books the first trench inspection (duct in place, before sand backfill) and later the second, in the construction inspectors' calendar.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Both inspections are booked through the Service Desk (trench page).

steps.name: Inspect the service trench and duct
steps.description: A construction inspector visits twice: first to check depth, width, duct size, rope and meter base conduit before the sand backfill, then after backfill. A failed inspection is written up and the contractor fixes it.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Conditions of Service s.2.1.5 and trench specification UDS0003: utility inspection of service ducts before and after backfill

evidence.note: Two inspections and trench specification from the trench page; utility inspection of ducts before backfill (Conditions of Service s.2.1.5). Minutes (two visits with travel) are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Contractor corrects the trench
steps.description: The contractor deepens the trench, replaces crushed duct or adds the missing rope, then calls the service desk again to book a re-inspection.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Create the work order and release it to scheduling
steps.description: The technologist builds the construction work order in the ERP with the material list (service wire, connectors, meter), attaches the layout sketch and inspection results, and releases it to work planning so the connection can be booked once the ESA authorization arrives.

error.defect_description: Material list or crew type wrong on the work order.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the hand-off to work planning follows the organisation file's process map.

exceptions.name: Missing information
exceptions.description: No site plan, service size or load summary; the request waits for the customer.

exceptions.name: Transformer or secondary upgrade needed
exceptions.description: The added load overloads the transformer or the secondary; an upgrade is designed and the customer is warned of material lead times.

exceptions.name: Customer does not proceed
exceptions.description: The customer drops the project or lets the 90-day quote expire.

exceptions.name: Revised layout
exceptions.description: The customer asks for a different meter location or service size after seeing the quote.

exceptions.name: Failed trench inspection
exceptions.description: Trench too shallow, duct crushed or rope missing; the contractor fixes it and calls for a re-inspection.

benchmarks.unit: business days from request to first call
benchmarks.population: Hydro Ottawa residential service requests (current published target)

evidence.note: Published service standard; the 2019-2022 practice is assumed similar.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from request to layout emailed

evidence.note: Hydro Ottawa asks customers to apply three to four weeks before the project; DSC s.6.1.1 allows 15 days to respond and 60 days to make an offer. Percentiles are the author's reading.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from request to work order released (cases that proceed)

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 2 to 4 weeks to the layout, then 2 to 12 weeks for the customer to pay and the electrician and trench contractor to finish.

pain_points.description: The same request is typed into the customer system and the ERP, and the designer re-reads the form and site plan from the document system.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of 2019-2022 system integration.

pain_points.description: Design queues build in spring and summer, so the first call and layout slip toward the 10-business-day and 15-day limits.

evidence.note: Published 10-business-day contact target and DSC 15-day response rule.

pain_points.description: Site visits take a technologist out for one to two hours per request, often only to confirm a meter location.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Trench inspections need two visits and fail when contractors do not follow the specification.

evidence.note: Two inspections per underground service.

assumptions: The process ends when the work order is released to work planning; booking the crew, the ESA authorization and the connection are in ops-service-connection-work.
Construction inspectors do the service trench inspections; the organisation file's process map lists only design technologists, supervisors and representatives for this process.
About half of the layouts are underground services that need trench inspections; overhead services and upgrades without a trench go straight to the work order.

The 10-business-day first-contact target and the 15-day and 60-day layout times come from Hydro Ottawa's current web pages and the 2026 Distribution System Code; the same sections (6.1.1, 7.3, 7.4) applied in 2019-2022.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's rates (wage x 1.40). FTEs add 15% to hands-on time for calls and revisions not tied to a step.

sources.title: What is a service connection inspection?
sources.supports: Service inspection after customer-owned service equipment is installed and before it is covered; ESA then authorizes the utility to energize; authorization valid up to six months; each project needs a service layout from the utility.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa Conditions of Service, ECS0012 Rev. 8 (proposed, effective December 2021)
sources.supports: s.2.1: design and material prepayments, deposits before field work; s.2.1.3: offer to connect contents, economic evaluation, expansion deposit (letter of credit, cash, surety), alternative bid with qualified contractors and 2-year warranty; s.2.1.5: ESA Connection Authorization Certificate required before energizing and must match address, voltage and ampacity; duct banks inspected before concrete and before backfill with a mandrel test, pads and vaults inspected before equipment; s.2.1.7: Installation and Service Agreement for developers; s.3.1.2: subdivision site information (plan, grading, phasing, load summary); s.3.1.3: utility designates supply point and meter base location, installs up to 30 m of service conductor, inspects service entry to the meter base; s.3.4: DER Form B, CIA fee, Installation and Service Agreement with Connection Cost Agreement, Hydro One consulted on the customer's behalf; Appendix G: quotes expire after 90 days, one free customer layout per property per year, two-person line crew isolations.

sources.title: Distribution system design
sources.supports: Distribution design handles commercial services over 50 kW, residential projects of five or more units and underground subdivisions; customer layouts cover infill of 50 kW or less; design and project management offered; designs must meet the Conditions of Service and OEB rules.

sources.title: Electrical service requests
sources.supports: Submit the service request form three to four weeks before the project; Hydro Ottawa calls within 10 business days; customer layout by email with initial site review and service loading assessment; customer pays the layout fees and then calls the Service Desk to schedule; extra charges if the site is not ready when the crew arrives; some projects take longer when equipment must be ordered.

sources.title: Contractors - Underground service trenches
sources.supports: Sequence for an underground service: customer layout, locate, trench, duct and rope, meter base, first inspection booked through the Service Desk, backfill with sand, second inspection, final backfill, ESA connection permit, then call the Service Desk to schedule the connection.

sources.title: Distribution System Code (last revised August 1, 2026)
sources.supports: s.6.1.1: respond to a written connection request within 15 calendar days and make an offer to connect within 60 calendar days; s.3.2 and Appendix B: economic evaluation, capital contribution, expansion deposit, alternative bid and final economic evaluation after energization; s.6.2.6: micro-embedded offer within 15, 30 or 60 days and at least 30 days to accept; s.6.2.7: connect a micro-embedded generator within 5 business days of ESA authorization, agreement and payment (90% of the time); s.6.2.9.1: preliminary consultation response within 15 days; s.6.2.12 and 6.2.13: CIA within 60, 75, 90 or 105 days; s.6.2.14A: file with the transmitter within 15 days; s.6.2.16: detailed cost estimate and offer to connect within 90 days of payment.

sources.title: Scorecard - Hydro Ottawa Limited (2017-2021) and 2021 Scorecard Management Discussion and Analysis
sources.supports: 5,024 new residential and small business services connected in 2021, 100% within five business days of conditions being met or as scheduled with the customer (DSC s.7.2, 90% minimum); 9,001 appointments for service upgrades, meter checks and service layouts in 2021 (98.86% on time, four-hour window under DSC s.7.4); missed appointments mainly caused by emergencies and weather; 6 CIAs totalling 11,635.8 kW in 2021 all on time, timelines 60 to 90 days, all CIA work done internally; 52 micro-embedded generators (10 kW or less) connected in 2021, 100% within five business days.
